correctness.rationale: For finite connected r- and s-regular components X and Y, the join decomposes into X transverse, Y transverse, and a two-dimensional uniform block Bγ; its λ± are distinct for γ>0, with λ+ greater than both degrees. Resolving λ−=μ gives exactly γμ=sqrt((r−μ)(s−μ)/(nm)) for X transverse eigenvalues μ<min(r,s); the Cesàro average of the fixed-sector amplitude contributes projector cross term (2β/n)Eμ only at these collisions. Each diagonal jump is nonnegative with strictly positive trace; cross-block average remains 2γ²/Δ² by orthogonality. The single vanishing phase gap derivative λ−′=−2γnm/Δ produces the uniform O_C(T^(-1)) sinc window for γ*=γμ+c/T, without treating finite time as discontinuous. For two equal cliques, independent direct three-phase pair averaging at n=2,3,7, γ=0.4,1,1.3, T=1,7.5,93 exactly reproduced the advertised closed finite-time formula. All-size claims rely on the invariant-sector algebra and isolated-gap estimate, not those samples.
